api_title_as_published: VCF Automation API | VM Apps Org - Catalog
why_not_a_specification: VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation.
The Apache-2.0 repository https://github.com/vmware/vcf-api-specs does not publish an OpenAPI document for VCF Automation; it covers other VCF components only.
No machine-readable OpenAPI document for the VCF Automation Catalog service is offered for download from the Broadcom Developer Portal.

Therefore docs/contract.json was transcribed by hand from the rendered reference pages listed below. It is a reading of documentation, not a projection of a published specification, and it is authoritative only for this exercise.

pages.documents: Service landing page for the VCF Automation Catalog API. Establishes the shared query conventions used across the service: page, size, sort, and the OData-style $top, $skip and $orderby, with the worked examples /catalog/api/items?$orderby=name%20desc, /catalog/api/items?$top=10&$skip=2 and /catalog/api/items?page=0&size=5.

GET /catalog/api/items - 'Get Catalog Items', summary 'Fetch a list of catalog items'. This is the sole operation the contract admits. Source for the full optional query parameter list (page default 0 zero-based, size default 20 minimum 1, sort as 'property,(asc|desc)', search, projects, types, expandProjects, expand, $top, $skip), for the bearer Authorization header, and for the PageCatalogItem 200 response.

PageCatalogItem response envelope: content, empty, first, last, number, numberOfElements, pageable, size, sort, totalElements, totalPages, plus the nested PageableObject (offset, pageNumber, pageSize, paged, sort, unpaged) and SortObject (empty, sorted, unsorted).

CatalogItem member list and, critically, which members are required: id, name, projectIds and type are required; description, sourceId, sourceName, createdAt, iconId, isRequestable, global, bulkRequestLimit, externalId, formId, schema, spec, projects, creator, lastUpdater, lastUpdatedAt, lastUpdatedBy, createdBy, additionalActions and organizationSharings are optional.

ResourceReference, the declared type of the required CatalogItem.type member. All four of its members - id, name, description, version - are documented as optional, which is why the contract requires the client to tolerate a type object that carries no id.

GET /catalog/api/admin/items - 'Get Catalog Items For Admin'. Recorded only to fix the boundary of the contract: it is a different route with a different parameter set (sourceIds, projectId) and is deliberately excluded, so the mock refuses it.

GET /catalog/api/items/{id} - 'Find a catalog item with specified ID'. Recorded only to fix the boundary of the contract: per-item lookup is excluded, so the collection must be assembled from the paginated route alone and the mock refuses this route.
